title: If you’re looking for PROOF that Aya Edebiri is a great actress- look...
transcript: Ayo Edebiri is giving a breathtaking performance in proof on Broadway. Her character, Catherine, is going through a lot. She has given up years of her life to care for her sick father basically by herself, and is now struggling to return to any kind of normalcy while also worrying that she may end up just as sick as her father was. Her character is somewhat aloof, and I always able to navigate this ambiguity with an extreme precision. We actually see her character in both flashback and present day, and I was really struck by how Ayo was able to make these two versions of the same character feel so distinct. Like, the second she came out for the first flashback, I was like, oh, this is a flashback, and she's younger. Just based on how she carried herself. And I'm surprised there hasn't been more hype around her, as I think this is one of the performances of the season. She is joined by a stellar supporting cast, including Don Cheadle as her father, who makes the most of his very limited stage time the always excellent kara Young as her sister Claire, in a much more serious role than we're used to seeing her, which is really fun. And Jin Ha as her father's former student and potential love interest, Harold Dobbs. But this is really Ayo's play, and she really carries it beautifully, which is incredibly impressive for her Broadway debut. The first act is definitely A bit of a slow burn. I was sitting there enjoying it, but also wondering, where is this going? And then the moment at the end of Act one happens, and you're like, oh, that's where this is going. Act 2 is this riveting payoff to everything that was just set up in Act 1. If I have one complaint about the production, it's that it lacks a clear directorial vision, as despite some strong performances, the overall production just feels a bit bland. There are also these clunky transitions that pretty much only exist so that the actors can go change costume. So I get why they're there, but they do slow down the pacing. But overall, I thought it was a really unique and well written play with enough twists and turns to keep me engaged. And that, combined with some really strong performances, definitely makes this a Broadway Ben recommendation.
